images.title: Letters for the missing boxes
images.purpose: Shows a four row pyramid with top 50 where the two missing bottom boxes are named p and q.
images.composition: One four row number pyramid in the centre, with two letter boxes and their values beside it.
images.exact_structure: Ten equal rectangular boxes stacked as a pyramid: 1 top box, 2 in the second row, 3 in the third row, 4 in the bottom row, each upper box centred over the join of the two below. Top box holds 50. Second row: left box empty, right box holds 22. Third row: three empty boxes. Bottom row, left to right: 4, p, 6, q. The boxes p and q are filled pale reddish purple #CC79A7 with dark italic letters; all other boxes have white fill and dark outline. To the right of the pyramid, two teal #0072B2 lines, one under the other: p = 9 and q = 1. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Name the boxes you cannot reach with letters, then solve for them.
images.description: Shows a four row pyramid with top 50 where the two missing bottom boxes are named p and q.
images.context: Picture for the four row pyramid with top 50.
images.teaching_notes: Two letters need two facts: the 22 gives p + q = 10, the 50 gives 3p + q = 28.

image_decisions.why: The pyramid layout shows which boxes are unknown and where the letters go, which words describe poorly.
